sources.title: BDUK delivery performance, annual: April 2025 to March 2026
facts: The annual official-statistics release covers BDUK-subsidised gigabit delivery between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026.
The release includes a bulletin, data tables, quality and methodology information and a pre-release access record.
The annual series revises previously reported delivery figures when newer supplier data are available.
Annual subsidy-attributable statistics are a different evidence family from monthly contract management snapshots.
Release metadata and observation period must be retained before trend comparison.

sources.title: Bulletin: BDUK delivery performance, annual April 2025 to March 2026
facts: BDUK estimated 192,570 premises delivered during 2025/26, 42,280 more than the previous financial year.
Cumulative gigabit-programme delivery reached an estimated 1,418,410 premises by March 2026.
GIS contracts accounted for 72% of annual delivery, vouchers 16%, and Superfast plus Hubs 12%.
Rural premises represented 90% of delivery during 2025/26.
The bulletin uses management information as of 15 May 2026 and multiple geographic lookup vintages.

sources.title: Quality and Methodology Information for BDUK delivery performance, annual April 2025 to March 2026
sources.lines: data, validation, classification, quality and revision sections
facts: The QMI documents data collection, validation, statistical processing and revision practices.
Classification systems and statistical concepts are documented separately from headline findings.
Accuracy, reliability, accessibility and burden are explicit quality dimensions.
Revisions are part of the official-statistics production process.
Methodology evidence cannot establish current service at an individual UPRN.

sources.title: Pre-release access list: BDUK delivery performance, annual April 2025 to March 2026
facts: The pre-release access list was published on 11 June 2026.
It records ministers and officials who received privileged early access.
The list is an official-statistics governance document rather than delivery evidence.
Pre-release access does not alter the observation period of the underlying statistics.
Governance metadata should remain linked to the associated annual release.

sources.title: Connected Nations - Planned Network Deployments 2026
sources.lines: report scope, confidence criteria and key findings
facts: The report examines planned full-fibre and gigabit-capable deployment through the end of 2028.
Plans reflect operator statements as of January 2026 and include private and publicly supported deployments.
Ofcom classifies plans as high confidence when low-level design is complete and funding is committed.
The report is forward-looking and supplements the January 2026 current-coverage snapshot.
Planned coverage cannot be promoted to current parcel availability.

sources.title: Connected Nations - Planned Network Deployment background
facts: The background page explains that PND reports supplement Connected Nations infrastructure reports.
The latest report covers operator plans over the three years following January 2026.
Fixed wireless access extension and upgrade plans are included.
Public-authority aspirations are not separately counted unless present in operator plans.
A planned-deployment record requires a current-coverage source before parcel promotion.

sources.title: May 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
facts: The May table is a BDUK snapshot dated 21 May 2026 and was updated on 20 July 2026.
It reports 837,340 contracted premises and 256,680 built contracted premises.
Supplier resubmissions reduced reported built counts for two contract areas pending revised data.
Figures are rounded to the nearest ten and are not contractual milestone evidence.
Monthly contracted and built data are not directly comparable with subsidy-attributable official statistics.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contracts collection
facts: The collection indexes local and regional Project Gigabit contracts awarded to suppliers.
Contract pages describe procurement scope, supplier and subsequent changes.
The collection includes contracts across England, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
Awarded scope is subject to planning, market change and contract redesign.
A contract listing is not proof that every listed premise can order service.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - Bedfordshire, Northamptonshire and Milton Keynes
sources.lines: May 2026 redesign and original contract details
facts: The May 2026 redesign reduced the stated scope from about 25,000 to about 6,000 premises.
The redesigned contract is backed by £19.8 million of Project Gigabit investment.
CityFibre is the named supplier.
The redesign was intended to reduce overlap with expanded commercial rollout.
Contract scope remains planning evidence rather than current service proof.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - Hampshire
sources.lines: May 2026 redesign and original contract details
facts: The May 2026 redesign revised the Hampshire scope to about 29,000 premises.
The redesigned contract is backed by £71.7 million of Project Gigabit investment.
CityFibre is the named supplier.
The original contract described about 75,500 premises and £104.2 million.
Build preparation and an awarded contract do not establish orderable service at each premise.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - Norfolk
sources.lines: May 2026 redesign and original contract details
facts: The May 2026 redesign revised Norfolk scope to about 33,000 premises.
The redesigned contract is backed by £61.9 million of Project Gigabit investment.
CityFibre is the named supplier.
The original contract described about 62,200 premises and £114.2 million.
Contract redesign reflects market conditions and cannot be treated as delivered coverage.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - Kent
facts: The original Kent contract was awarded to CityFibre.
The original scope was about 50,000 hard-to-reach premises.
The original contract value was £112 million and it was signed in January 2024.
The page was updated on 26 May 2026.
Detailed planning and subsequent technical changes can alter premises scope.
